Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

distmer 0.9.4

distmer 0.9.3

Version 0.9.3 extends unbalanced nested inference to hierarchies of any depth and to any number of fixed terms, adds calibration validators for the mixed engines introduced in 0.9.2, and corrects a series of numerical-conditioning defects found while doing so.

Results change for two engines. permanova_unbalanced_nested() now averages child centroids with equal weight, and permutation p-values are corrected wherever an absolute comparison tolerance had made them too small; see “Multi-level unbalanced nested designs” and “Extremeness comparison used an absolute tolerance” below.

Crossed mixed designs with empty cells or unequal replication

  • New engine permanova_crossed_incomplete(), reached automatically from permanova() when a crossed mixed design is not a complete, equally replicated factorial. Previously such a design was refused outright: permanova_crossed() requires every cell present and every cell the same size, and the unbalanced fixed engine separately refuses rank deficiency, so a field experiment revisited on different schedules at different sites had no route through the package at all.
  • Degrees of freedom are estimable dimensions, not level-count products. With s sites, t times and only c of the s*t cells occupied, the site-by-time interaction spans c - s - t + 1 dimensions rather than (s-1)(t-1). The table reports what the term can actually estimate and carries nominal_df alongside, so the loss is visible rather than silent; $rank_deficient names the affected terms.
  • Sums of squares are marginal, under sum-to-zero coding. Each term is compared against the model holding every term that does not contain it. Dropping a term’s columns from the full model – the obvious construction – is the wrong comparison here: a term containing this one spans it, so with the site-by-time interaction still fitted, removing the site columns removes nothing and site reports zero degrees of freedom. In a complete design the higher-order contrasts are orthogonal to the margin and the question never arises, which is why the balanced engine can drop columns safely.
  • Denominators are matched from the design’s expected mean squares under the restricted parameterisation, so a fixed term crossed with a random factor is tested over the stratum carrying the same random components and falls back to a Satterthwaite combination when imbalance leaves no single stratum matching. The restriction applies on both sides: a random stratum carries no component from a random-by-fixed interaction inside it, and a fixed term’s own expected mean square carries only the components whose fixed factors are exactly its own – E(MS_bird) holds the bird-by-time component but not site-by-bird-by-time. Without the second rule a random term would be matched against itself and return a pseudo-F of exactly one.
  • Continuous covariates are carried as slopes rather than factors, so a covariate costs one degree of freedom instead of one per distinct value.
  • Nesting is told apart from crossing when deciding which random components belong in a term’s expected mean square. A random term written treatment:chamber names the treatment only because chamber is nested inside it, whereas treatment:chamber:time is genuinely crossed with time. Reading the label literally put time over the residual instead of over chamber(treatment) x time; the test is now whether the fixed factor is determined by the term’s other variables.
  • Interaction terms are matched by their variable set rather than their written order, since terms() can return chamber:time as time:chamber.
  • Random terms are optional. With none the engine covers the incomplete fixed design, which permanova()’s Type III fixed path refuses outright (“aliased columns from incomplete cells”): every stratum collapses to the residual and each term is tested over it, while the rank-based construction reports what the empty cells leave estimable.
  • hypothesis selects the sums of squares: "II" (default) adjusts each term for every term that does not contain it, "I" is sequential, "III" adjusts for every other term in the model. On a complete equally replicated design all three coincide. On an incomplete one they do not, and Type III is the one to be careful with: a term containing this one can span it, so a main effect can report zero estimable degrees of freedom. Type II is the default because it stays well posed however incomplete the design is.
  • The correctness anchor is agreement. On a complete, equally replicated design both this engine and the validated permanova_crossed() apply, and they return identical degrees of freedom, sums of squares and pseudo-F to machine precision. Everything else is that same construction carried into designs the balanced engine refuses.

Multi-level unbalanced nested designs

  • permanova(d ~ terms... + (1 | region/site/quadrat)) now works when replication is unequal at more than one level, via a new engine permanova_unbalanced_nested_multi(). Previously only a single parent/child pair was supported, and deeper unbalanced chains were refused.
  • The engine takes any number of fixed terms, closing an asymmetry in the package: multi-factor support already existed for an unbalanced (1 | unit) design through permanova_unbalanced_splitplot(), but every unbalanced nested engine accepted exactly one categorical factor, so ~ A + B + (1 | reg/site) or ~ A * B + (1 | reg/site/quad) was refused. Each term is now assigned to the shallowest hierarchy level within which it is constant and tested there, with Type I/II/III partitioning among the terms sharing a level. A term that varies inside the deepest unit – typically an observation-level covariate – is tested over the within-unit residual with residuals permuted within those units. Verified against independent lm references at every level: region, site, and observation, including interactions, and against car::Anova for the Type III partition.
  • Permutation moves intact units within their own parent and only across units whose complete subtree shape matches, generalising the parent/child engine’s sorted-child-count rule. Treatment contrasts not spanned by that restricted action reject rather than being tested invalidly.
  • Behaviour change. permanova_unbalanced_nested() now uses the same cascaded aggregation, so a parent centroid averages its child centroids with equal weight instead of averaging the parent’s observations directly. The two agreed already when children were equally replicated; under unequal child replication the pseudo-F, and any p-value derived from it, will differ from 0.9.1. The observation-weighted parent centroid let a child carrying more replicates pull its parent, which is the imbalance the equal-weight estimand exists to remove, and it disagreed with the deeper chains. Top-level unbalanced-nested contrasts inherit the same change. Engines with no level between the aggregation unit and the observations (permanova_unequal_random_intercept(), permanova_unbalanced_block(), and the child/observation-level nested engine) are unaffected, since for them the two conventions coincide.
  • Because that change moves published numbers and a NEWS entry is easy to miss, an affected fit now says so in its own warnings. The note is raised only when children really are unequally replicated within a parent; when they are not, the old and new conventions coincide and there is nothing to report.

Denominators derived from the design’s expected mean squares

  • permanova_asymmetric_mixed() applied the balanced-design rule – whole-plot terms over the unit stratum, sub-plot terms over the unit-by-sub-plot stratum – to designs that are not balanced. The package elsewhere promises never to invent an unbalanced expected mean square; this engine did so implicitly, and on a reef survey with island sizes from 2 to 240 sites it put six of seven fixed terms out by 25 to 95 per cent.
  • A new denominator argument (default "ems") derives the expected mean squares of the numerator and of every candidate stratum from the actual design by the trace method, then constructs the ratio from them. Where the match would need a negative coefficient on the residual, the surplus is moved to the numerator rather than truncated, keeping every coefficient non-negative, and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom apply to both sides – so a numerator df need not be a whole number. denominator = "stratum" restores the previous rule.
  • Balanced designs give an exact single-stratum match and are unchanged.
  • The interaction covariance component is orthogonalised against the unit main effect. Without it no random component is attributable to a single stratum, the construction has no solution, and the engine silently falls back.
  • Validated against a published PRIMER workspace for an unbalanced three-stratum design: the construction reproduces PRIMER’s pseudo-F, numerator df and denominator df for every fixed term to all printed digits, and the trace-derived EMS coefficients match PRIMER’s to five significant figures. Within the engine the mean absolute log ratio against PRIMER falls from 0.335 to 0.037.

Contrasts within the cells of other factors

  • permanova_contrasts_within() contrasts the levels of one fixed factor inside every combination of others, as PRIMER’s “within level” pairwise tables do.
  • The denominator cannot be inherited from the parent fit. Inside one cell the lower strata often collapse – an ecoregion sampled on two islands leaves the unit-by-sub-plot stratum with no degrees of freedom – so each pair rebuilds the declared random strata on its own subset, drops those with no degrees of freedom, and matches the contrast’s expected mean square against the survivors. Three pairs inside one cell can therefore carry three different denominators and three different Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, which no single fitted model can produce.
  • Residuals are permuted inside the experimental unit, so observations move between the levels being contrasted.
  • Expected mean squares are restricted, as PRIMER’s are. PRIMER states the convention in its workspace header – “Fixed effects sum to zero for mixed terms” – and under that restricted model the mean square of a random stratum carries no variance component from a random-by-fixed interaction nested inside it: E(MS_island) contains no island-by-depth component, though E(MS_island x depth) does. distmer previously used the unrestricted accounting and then tried to recover the zero by orthogonalising the interaction’s Z against the containing stratum, which is the wrong instrument: it changes that component’s covariance everywhere it appears, including in the contrast’s own expected mean square, and left the inner coefficient too small by up to 18 per cent. The zero now goes where it belongs, in the stratum’s row of the accounting, and a component’s covariance is ZZ' as declared.
  • Permutation happens at the level of the denominator’s finest stratum. When a denominator is carried by a grouping stratum rather than the residual, the exchangeable entity is a whole unit of that stratum – an island-by-depth cell – not an observation. Permuting observations inside the island instead treats every sample in a cell as an independent replicate; that is pseudo-replication, and it made p-values too small in 19 of 20 affected contrasts. Units of unequal size cannot be permuted as rows, so the exchange is done on unit centroids. This costs nothing: any projector constant within units satisfies tr(H L G L') = tr(H G), so the observed statistic is unchanged and only the null moves. Residuals are permuted under a reduced model holding the coarser strata, weighted by unit size.
  • The numerator’s surplus residual reaches the permutation. Where the matched weights carry more than one unit of residual, the construction moves the surplus onto the numerator rather than allowing a negative weight, so the statistic is (numerator MS + surplus * residual MS) / denominator. The permutation was computing the numerator mean square alone, leaving the null on a different scale from the observed statistic it was compared against. Both permutation paths now carry the surplus, and the unit-level path asserts that the unpermuted configuration reproduces the reported statistic exactly, so the two cannot drift apart again unnoticed.
  • Validated against the same PRIMER workspace, now on all 27 contrasts in the complete within-level table rather than one cell. Every t statistic, every denominator coefficient on all three strata, and every Satterthwaite degree of freedom reproduces to PRIMER’s printed precision, and the calls at the five per cent level are identical throughout.

Known gap: the within-cell null over a grouping stratum

Where the residual carries a within-cell denominator, the exchangeable unit is the observation and the permutation p-values match PRIMER’s to within 0.007.

Where a grouping stratum carries it, the exchangeable unit is a whole unit of that stratum. distmer now permutes the right space – PRIMER’s own unique-perm counts name it exactly at 720 = 6! for a cell with six occupied island-by-depth units, and distmer finds the same 720 – but the distribution over that space is not yet identical to PRIMER’s. Gaps reach 0.157 on 18 such contrasts, mean 0.037, with distmer the more conservative of the two in 15 of 18.

Fixing the surplus-residual defect above moved these p-values away from PRIMER, not toward it: the closer agreement beforehand was an artifact of the null being on the wrong scale. Five variants of the statistic and the reduced model were tested against the nine contrasts where both sides can be enumerated exactly, and none accounts for the difference, so the cause is not one of those choices. The tests bound this discrepancy rather than asserting agreement. - permanova_contrasts() reaches this family directly, via a new within = argument. Naming several factors in factor is shorthand for the same thing: the first is contrasted inside combinations of the rest, and the reading taken is reported. Several factors cannot mean contrasting their crossed cells – two cells of a crossed combination leave the design’s lower strata with no degrees of freedom – so the shorthand is unambiguous. within is refused for the non-pairwise families, which need a contrast matrix over all levels that a single cell need not carry, and for method = "pooled", which has no meaning when every pair derives its own denominator. - The result prints grouped by cell, so a within-level table can be read as published.

Whole-plot terms were untestable on unequally replicated designs

  • permanova_asymmetric_mixed() permutes whole units by swapping blocks of observation indices, which is only defined between units holding the same counts in the same sub-plot classes. Real surveys give every unit a distinct count vector: in a 33-island reef dataset all 33 signatures were unique, so no two islands were exchangeable, the only attainable arrangement was the identity, and every whole-plot term returned p = 1.0000 regardless of its pseudo-F. A term with pseudo-F of 26 was reported as p = 1.
  • A new whole_plot argument decides what happens. "observation" keeps the intact-unit action at the observation level, weighting units by how many observations they carry – the estimand the IS(unit) stratum defines. "centroid" tests whole-plot terms on equally weighted unit centroids and permutes units freely, so a p-value exists for any design. "auto" (the default) uses the observation-level action whenever any two units are exchangeable and falls back to centroids otherwise.
  • The two agree exactly when units are equally replicated, so no existing balanced analysis moves; a regression test pins that bit-for-bit. Under imbalance they target different estimands, and a fit that fell back says so in the affected terms’ warnings. The action taken is recorded on the fit as $whole_plot.
  • The unit-level denominator is the residual among unit centroids after every whole-plot term, so all whole-plot tests share one denominator exactly as they do at the observation level.
  • Sub-plot terms are untouched: they keep the observation-level action and the unit-by-sub-plot stratum.

Permutation resolution reaches the asymmetric engine

  • permanova_asymmetric_mixed() computed the resolution diagnostic and then discarded it, so the p = 1.0000 above arrived with no explanation. It now reports distinct_statistics and minimum_attainable_p on every test spec and raises the resolution warning, which names exactly this failure (“the permutation distribution holds only 1 distinct statistic”). Progress bars in this engine were also unlabelled, so a multi-term fit drew several anonymous bars; each is now labelled with its term and denominator stratum.

Calibration validators for the newer mixed engines

  • Five engines had unit tests but no entry in the validation harness. Each now has a simulate_*_validation() function pinned to an independently computed classical reference, and run_permanova_validation() checks that agreement: permanova_mixed_covariate() against aov(y ~ tr * sub + Error(unit)); permanova_unbalanced_splitplot() against an lm on equally weighted unit centroids; permanova_nested_covariate() against SS(factor | covariate) over the factor-only nested stratum; permanova_asymmetric_mixed() against aov(y ~ EC * DE + Error(ISLAND / DE)); and permanova_random_slope_continuous() against a one-sample test on per-group slopes. All agree to better than 1e-13.
  • Type-I error at 300 simulations is within Monte-Carlo error of the nominal 0.05 for all five (0.037-0.060; every 95% interval covers 0.05).

Restricted permutation with a singleton stratum

  • .stratified_permutation_plan() used sample(position), which permutes seq_len(x) when x is a single number. A permutation stratum containing exactly one unit therefore aborted the fit (“number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length”) unless that unit happened to be the first observation. Singleton strata are common in unbalanced data – one unit with a unique replicate count, or one hierarchy unit with a unique topology – and every engine using restricted permutation was affected, including permanova_unequal_random_intercept(), permanova_unbalanced_splitplot(), permanova_asymmetric_mixed(), and the unbalanced nested engines. The stratum is now indexed explicitly and a singleton is correctly held fixed.

Nesting chains crossed with unrelated random factors

  • permanova() refused designs such as ~ tr + (1 | a/b) + (1 | c) only after routing them into the crossed engine, which reported an internal “Phase 3” message about /-generated nesting. The dispatcher now refuses the structure directly, names the nesting chain involved, and points to either the nested engine or the validated crossed-nested hybrid form.

Degenerate results from a model with no testable fixed term

  • A design whose fixed terms are all absorbed by the random structure produced permutation$used = -Inf and an internal warning (“no non-missing arguments to max”) instead of a clean zero. Three of the four sites taking the maximum over an empty set of test specifications lacked the guard the fourth already had; all four now agree.

Extremeness comparison used an absolute tolerance

  • Permutation p-values counted a statistic as extreme when it reached observed - tol with tol = 1e-10 absolute. The identity permutation reproduces the observed statistic only up to floating-point rounding, and at a pseudo-F of around 1e4 that rounding is roughly 1e-9 – larger than the tolerance. The permutation that should always tie with the observed value then failed to count, and an exhaustive test could report p = 0, which no permutation test can legitimately produce. In one four-unit design the reported p-value was 0 where the correct exact value is 1/3.
  • Widening the slack alone was not enough. The observed statistic and its permuted counterparts are reached by different arithmetic paths, and under severe conditioning – a pseudo-F of 1e12, say – the tie between them is lost by more than any fixed relative slack. Under exact enumeration the identity permutation is a member of the set and always ties, so p >= 1/N holds as a theorem; that bound is now enforced directly, which removes the whole class regardless of how well conditioned the design is.
  • The comparison also now scales with the magnitude of the observed statistic in every engine, using the same sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) floor the package already applies to numerical-equality checks. p-values are unchanged on ordinary scales – verified identical to the previous idiom across 200 randomised cases – and are corrected upward wherever the statistic was large enough for the old slack to fail. Designs with well-separated groups are the ones affected, so any previously reported p-value of exactly 0 should be recomputed.

Numerically-zero guards are now scale free

  • Sixteen guards across twelve engines refused a fit when a mean square was “numerically zero”, comparing it with an absolute tol = 1e-10. A mean square carries the squared units of the dissimilarity, so that test was not scale free: the same analysis was accepted on a response of ordinary magnitude and refused after multiplying the response by 1e-4. Data already on a small scale – proportions, or an already-normalised dissimilarity – could be rejected with “the … mean square is numerically zero” when nothing was wrong with it. This was reported as a known limitation in 0.9.3.
  • Each guard now measures the mean square against the total inertia of the same Gower matrix, so the question becomes “is this stratum negligible relative to the variation in these data”, which is what the guard is for and does not depend on the units of the response.

Consistent refusal of a degenerate denominator

  • permanova_oneway() and permanova_fixed() divided by a numerically zero residual and returned an infinite pseudo-F, while every other engine refused. Both now refuse with the same message. Only the observed statistic is guarded, so a single degenerate permutation cannot abort an otherwise valid run.
  • permanova_oneway() gains a tol argument for that check.

Permutation resolution is now reported

  • A restricted permutation scheme can attain many arrangements yet produce only a handful of distinct statistics: permuting labels inside a treatment group leaves the statistic untouched. Two groups of two attain 24 arrangements but only three distinct pseudo-F values, so the smallest p-value the design can return is a third – however large the effect. Reporting the count of attainable arrangements alone hid this.
  • Test specifications now carry distinct_statistics and minimum_attainable_p, and a design that cannot reach the chosen level however large its effect says so in its warnings. The level is the new distmer.resolution_alpha option (default 0.05); it is a reporting threshold only, and the two numbers are recorded whatever it is set to.
  • A new ?\distmer-options`help page documents every option that changes how the package reports --distmer.resolution_alpha,distmer.progress, anddistmer.progress_min`. None of them changes an inferential result. The progress options existed since 0.9.2 but were only described in an internal comment.
  • The p-value computation itself, previously duplicated at two dozen sites, is now a single shared helper, which is what let both of the above be fixed in one place.

Models with no fixed term

  • permanova() now refuses a formula whose only terms are random, instead of returning a sums-of-squares table with no statistic in it. The refusal names the estimator that does decompose a pure random structure – estimate_nested_variance_components() for a /-generated chain, estimate_variance_components() otherwise – and suggests a concrete repair using the user’s own grouping factor.
  • estimate_nested_variance_components() no longer requires a fixed term. The requirement came from a validator shared with the testing path, where it is correct; the estimator itself never used the fixed model. With no fixed terms each stratum is simply left unadjusted, which is the correct pure random-effects decomposition, and the result now reproduces the classical nested analysis-of-variance components exactly.
  • The “Only random effects” section of the random-effects vignette previously claimed an error was thrown but illustrated it with ~ (1 + period), which parses as a fixed term and would not have errored. It now shows the real refusal and the variance-component route.

Removal of abandoned internal helpers

  • Six never-called internal functions (.fix1_partial_term, .fix2_distinct_perms, .fix3_confounded, .fix3_no_test_row, .fix4_classify_grouping, .fix5_no_fixed_message) have been deleted. Each duplicated a policy the live code already implements, in most cases less safely: the grouping classifier counted distinct levels per group where the live classifier uses projection ranks, and the no-test table row used column names that do not match any table the package builds.

Capability registry completeness

  • The registry returned by permanova_capabilities() was missing five routable engines (permanova_mixed_covariate, permanova_unbalanced_splitplot, permanova_nested_covariate, permanova_asymmetric_mixed, and permanova_random_slope_continuous). All are now registered, along with the new multi-level nested engine, and inst/SUPPORT-MATRIX.md names each one.
  • A release-audit test now reads the engine names out of permanova()’s own dispatcher and fails if any routable engine is absent from the registry, so the contract cannot drift again. The registry-size checks in the validation harness and unit tests no longer pin an exact count.

Documentation

  • The random-effects vignette gains two sections. “Nested hierarchies with unequal effort” works a (1 | region/site/quadrat) survey in which quadrat effort differs between survey rounds, showing each fixed term being tested at the level where it varies and explaining what a centroid means when effort is unequal. “What a permutation design can and cannot resolve” uses the same fit to show a restricted scheme attaining 576 arrangements but only 18 distinct pseudo-F values, so that the p-value cannot fall below 0.056 whatever the effect size – and points at ?`distmer-options` for the reporting level.
  • Neither the multi-level nested engine nor the resolution diagnostic had any user-facing documentation before this.
  • The same vignette now opens with two scope tables: the random structures that are covered, with what each fixed term is tested against, and those that are not yet covered, with what to reach for instead. The boundary is two independent random structures at once – one hierarchy of any depth is well covered, but a slope alongside another random term, or two crossed hierarchies, are not. Crossed random factors are listed as a partial case: the pseudo-F, EMS and variance components are available, only the permutation p-value is not.

distmer 0.9.2

Version 0.9.2 consolidates the complete post-0.9.1 development tree: the low-rank Freedman–Lane refactor, progress reporting, asymmetric three-stratum mixed models, balanced and unbalanced multi-factor split-plots, and the fit-based contrasts API. The adversarial corrections below are part of the same reviewed source snapshot.

Adversarial inference hardening

  • Exact asymmetric-mixed and split-plot requests now enumerate their complete restricted spaces instead of returning zero permutations and NA p-values.
  • Incomplete asymmetric units move only within identical subplot-count topologies, and unequal split-plot units move only within exact-size strata.
  • Fit-based isolated contrasts retain the complete original formula, random effects, nuisance terms, denominator, and permutation action.

Low-rank Freedman–Lane permutation

  • Every residual-permutation engine now shares one kernel (.freedman_lane_kernel()) instead of forming the permuted Gower matrix A %*% G %*% t(A) explicitly. Expanding that product leaves the reduced-model projector and the cross terms as fixed matrices, so only R G R is re-indexed by each permutation; factoring each hypothesis projector as W diag(s) W' then reduces a permutation to one narrow matrix product with r columns, where r is the hypothesis rank. Residual projectors, whose rank is close to n, are carried through their complement using the fact that permutation similarity leaves tr(R G R) unchanged. Cost per permutation falls from O(n^3) to O(n^2 r): roughly 11x faster at n = 160, 20x at n = 320, and 18x at n = 1000. Results are unchanged to machine precision (relative difference below 1e-13) and the random-number stream is untouched, so seeded p-values reproduce exactly. Engines covered: permanova_mixed(), permanova_nested(), permanova_unbalanced(), permanova_mixed_covariate(), permanova_nested_covariate(), permanova_unequal_random_intercept(), permanova_unbalanced_nested(), permanova_unbalanced_nested_lower(), permanova_unbalanced_block(), permanova_unbalanced_splitplot(), permanova_asymmetric_mixed(), and every contrast family built on them.
  • permanova_dispersion() evaluates its rank-one permuted response as the quadratic form z'Hz rather than building the n-by-n outer product.

Permutation progress reporting

  • Long permutation runs now draw a text progress bar labelled with the term or contrast being permuted. Reporting is off outside an interactive session and is suppressed below 200 permutations, so scripts, tests, vignettes, and R CMD check are unaffected. Set options(distmer.progress = TRUE) to force it on (or FALSE to silence it), and options(distmer.progress_min = ) to change the length at which a run is worth reporting.

Asymmetric nested mixed designs (three error strata)

  • permanova(distance ~ fixed... + (1 | unit) + (1 | unit:subplot)) now routes to a new engine, permanova_asymmetric_mixed(), reproducing PRIMER’s asymmetric nested mixed design with three observation-level error strata: whole-plot fixed effects (not involving the sub-plot factor) tested over the unit stratum IS(unit); sub-plot fixed effects tested over the unit-by-sub-plot interaction stratum subplot x IS(unit); and both random strata tested over the residual. Fixed-term sums of squares are standard full-model Type I/II/III; the whole-plot vs sub-plot classification only selects the denominator. Degrees of freedom are derived from the actual (possibly incomplete) design. For the Caribbean benthos example this is bray ~ DEPTH * ECOREGION * POP_STATUS + (1 | ISLAND) + (1 | ISLAND:DEPTH), giving IS(EC x PS) (whole-plot denominator) and DE x IS(EC x PS) (sub-plot denominator) – the ST5 structure. Validated to reproduce aov(y ~ DE*EC*PS + Error(ISLAND/DE)) exactly for every fixed term F, the stratum degrees of freedom, and the residual. (The two-stratum permanova_unbalanced_splitplot() remains for designs without a random unit-by-sub-plot interaction.)

Unbalanced multi-factor split-plot designs

  • permanova(distance ~ f1 + f2 + ... + (1 | unit)) now works when the units are unequally replicated, via a new engine permanova_unbalanced_splitplot(). Whole-plot factors (constant within each unit) are tested on equally weighted unit centroids over the between-unit stratum – the unit-weighted estimand of permanova_unequal_random_intercept() generalised to any number of fixed factors and Type I/II/III sums of squares – with size-restricted whole-unit permutation. Within-unit (sub-plot) factors and between-by-within interactions are tested over the within-unit residual with within-unit residual permutation. This is the distance-based analogue of PRIMER’s asymmetric nested design (e.g. IS(EC x PS) as the whole-plot stratum and DE x IS(EC x PS) as the sub-plot residual) for unequally sampled units. The permanova() front door routes a balanced design to permanova_mixed_covariate() and an unbalanced one here; a lone whole-plot factor still uses permanova_unequal_random_intercept(). Validated to reproduce, exactly, an lm on equal-weight unit centroids for the whole-plot terms, a unit-blocked lm for the sub-plot terms, the balanced split-plot engine when balanced, and the single-factor unit-centroid engine.

Multi-factor split-plot and randomized-block mixed designs (no covariate needed)

  • The single-random-intercept engine no longer requires exactly one fixed factor or that the factor be constant within the unit. permanova(distance ~ f1 + f2 + ... (+ interactions) + (1 | unit)) now supports any number of fixed factors, each classified relative to the random unit and tested over the matching stratum: whole-plot factors (constant within every unit) over the between-unit stratum; within-unit sub-plot / randomized-block factors (fully crossed within every unit) and between-by-within interactions over the within-unit residual. A partially confounded factor (neither constant nor fully crossed within the unit) is refused rather than given a wrong denominator. A continuous covariate remains optional and is handled as before, including a between-unit covariate (constant within units), which is treated as a whole-plot term.
  • permanova_mixed_covariate() (still the engine, now covariate-optional) is documented as the general split-plot / randomized-block / ANCOVA engine. permanova() routes the simple single-whole-plot-factor case to the exact-EMS permanova_mixed() and everything richer to this engine. Validated to reproduce aov(y ~ ... + Error(unit)) and the blocked linear model exactly for whole-plot factors, sub-plot factors, and between-by-within interactions. This realises and validates an earlier internal split-plot design sketch, now removed.

Fit-based contrasts API

  • permanova_contrasts() now operates on a fitted permanova() object (rather than a compiled design), with contrast families via contrast_matrix() and two testing methods: "isolated" (a validated two-group subset test) and "pooled" (whose pseudo-F equals the classical constrained-scalar contrast F, verified to machine precision). permanova_pairwise() is removed – permanova_contrasts(fit, type = "pairwise") replaces it. The validation suite and capability registry were updated to the new API. Shared internal helpers (%||%, .stopf, .warnf) are consolidated in one utils.R.

distmer 0.9.0.9000

Versioning reset before the first stable release

  • The active package version is now 0.9.0.9000: a pre-release development line leading to the first stable 1.0.0 release.
  • Earlier version-like numbers were internal implementation checkpoints, not published package releases. Their detailed notes remain below for audit traceability but are explicitly labelled as unreleased checkpoints.
  • Four-component .9000 versions are development snapshots. The public release will use 1.0.0, with later releases following semantic versioning.

The source previously carrying the internal 2.9.1.9000 label was renumbered to 0.9.0.9000; this is a version-policy correction, not a rollback of code or validated capability.

Mixed-covariate and asymptotic-inference hardening

  • Rebuilt the documentation as a seven-guide ecological workflow: an explicit distance-based mixed-model introduction, fixed effects, pairwise contrasts, distance and dispersion diagnostics, unbalanced designs, random effects, and reproducible validation. Worked examples now use vegan::dune, vegan::mite, and vegan::pyrifos, with ggplot2 figures. Implementation routing is kept as a secondary reference in the random-effects guide.

  • Mixed and nested covariate projectors now use scale-aware stratum projection, so structurally zero between/within components cannot acquire numerical rank. Single-random-intercept models assign a numeric term that is constant within groups to the between-group stratum. Nested covariate inference rejects a numeric term with no deepest-stratum variation because that higher-level term requires a denominator outside the supported envelope.

  • Nested covariate Type I/II/III hypotheses now apply to covariate main effects and slope interactions as well as factors. Their Freedman–Lane reduced model retains every term used to adjust the observed numerator.

  • Balanced random-intercept inference now honours Type I/II/III fixed-effect hypotheses instead of coupling the numerator partition to the random-effect denominator choice.

  • P(MC) now derives its eigenvalue spectrum from each test’s orthogonal numerator-plus-denominator stratum. Variation outside that stratum can no longer change an upper-level mixed-model p-value.

  • permanova_mixed_covariate(permutations = "all") now enumerates the actual whole-group or within-group action, respects max_exact, and reports its finite attainable space.

  • Continuous random-slope sign-flip inference remains available with unequal covariate information. The parametric F(1, ng - 1) reference is now limited to rank-one Euclidean slopes with equal within-group SSx; the slope variance component subtracts MS[Residual] * mean(1 / SSx).

  • The source release audit scans all Rd files and the current seven-vignette series. Development handoff and readiness documents now follow the active version rather than the retired Phase 28 tree.

Internal checkpoint label: 2.9.0.9000 (unreleased).

Type I / II / III sums of squares for the fixed part of mixed designs

  • The type argument of permanova() now applies to the covariate-adjusted mixed engines, not only pure fixed-effect models. permanova_mixed_covariate() and permanova_nested_covariate() gained a hypothesis argument ("I" sequential, "II" marginal/containment-respecting, "III" partial), threaded from the front-door type. The sum-of-squares type changes only how each fixed term’s numerator reduced model is formed; the random-structure denominator is unchanged. Types coincide for an orthogonal balanced fixed structure and differ only when the fixed terms are non-orthogonal (crossed factors with unequal cell counts). Validated against car::Anova: for a block design with an unbalanced within-block A*B structure, distmer reproduces the Type I, Type II, and (through the front door’s automatic sum-to-zero contrasts) Type III F ratios exactly. The front door no longer warns that type is ignored for these engines.

Internal checkpoint label: 2.8.0.9000 (unreleased).

Covariate adjustment for single random-intercept designs (split-plot / RCB ANCOVA)

  • permanova(distance ~ factor + covariate + (1 | group)) now routes to a new engine, permanova_mixed_covariate(), extending covariate adjustment beyond the balanced nested engine to the single-random-intercept case. Each fixed term is classified by whether it varies within the grouping unit: between-unit (whole-plot) factors are tested over the between-group random-intercept stratum, while within-unit terms – sub-plot or randomized-block factors, observation-level covariates, and covariate-by-factor slope interactions – are tested over the within-group residual. This is the distance-based split-plot and randomized-block analysis of covariance. Unlike permanova_nested_covariate(), it removes the covariate’s between-unit component from the factor denominator and adjusts each whole-plot factor for the covariate’s between-unit slope (which differs from the pooled slope), so a covariate with between-unit structure is handled correctly without a manual decompose_covariate() step. Validated to reproduce the whole-plot factor test against aov(y ~ covariate + factor + Error(group)) and the within-unit (sub-plot factor, covariate, slopes) tests against the corresponding blocked linear model, exactly, including degrees of freedom.

Internal checkpoint label: 2.7.0.9000 (unreleased).

Continuous-covariate random slopes

  • permanova(distance ~ x + (1 + x | group)) with a numeric x now routes to a new engine, permanova_random_slope_continuous(), for the covariate-by- random model of Anderson, Gorley & Clarke (2008, Fig. 1.48b). The fixed slope has no exact single-source denominator in the full observation space (its expected mean square mixes the random-slope and residual components with different coefficients), so the test aggregates – exactly as the two-level categorical engine reduces to per-subject difference vectors – to one within-group slope vector per group, then tests the equally weighted mean slope against the between-group slope variation by whole-group sign flips, with a parametric F(1, ng - 1) p-value for Euclidean dissimilarities. For a balanced design this is the exact two-stage slope test, validated to reproduce it to machine precision and to agree closely with lmerTest. The earlier attempt to build this denominator with structured_denominator() was abandoned: the differing expected-mean-square coefficients inflated the synthesised denominator and pushed the pseudo-F ~1.6x below both gold standards, whereas the aggregated slope-vector test matches them exactly.
  • permanova_random_slope() (the balanced two-level categorical sign-flip engine) now rejects a continuous slope variable with a message pointing to the continuous engine, instead of failing obscurely.

Internal checkpoint label: 2.6.0.9000 (unreleased).

Monte-Carlo asymptotic p-value: P(MC)

  • permanova() now reports P(MC) alongside P(perm) for designs tested in the full observation space (fixed, balanced mixed, nested, crossed, hybrid). Following McArdle & Anderson (2001) and Anderson & Robinson (2003), the numerator and denominator sums of squares are drawn from the eigenvalue- weighted chi-square distribution implied by the Gower matrix, so the p-value stays smooth when the true permutation space is tiny – the usual situation for the upper strata of a mixed design, where restricted permutation yields very few unique arrangements. It reduces exactly to the classical F distribution in the univariate Euclidean limit; validated against aov() for a one-way design and against the exact balanced-mixed F-test over its stratum. Controlled by mc_permutations (default 9999; set 0 to disable) and reproducible from seed. Aggregated-unit engines (random slope, unequal random intercept, unbalanced nested/hybrid) test in a reduced centroid space where the full-matrix asymptotics do not hold, so their P(MC) is left NA.

PRIMER-style nested containment labels

  • Covariate-adjusted nested summaries now label strata with PRIMER containment notation (Site(Location), Area(Site(Location)), Residual) in the table, the denominators, and the V() variance components, derived from the design’s nesting rather than hard-coded. The estimates of components of variation are reported in a single PRIMER-style block with S() fixed-effect sizes and V() random variance components.

Internal checkpoint label: 2.5.0.9000 (unreleased).

Structured mixed-model denominators

  • Added structured_denominator(), a Cornfield–Tukey / Satterthwaite denominator constructor that synthesises mean squares in containment-lattice order rather than by the minimum-norm match used in quasi_denominator(). On a clean balanced design it returns the exact single-source denominator; on a perturbed (e.g. random-slope) design it returns the structured combination with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. Validated against the clean balanced limit and against lmerTest denominator df (the latter requires the covariate to be within-centred, e.g. via decompose_covariate(), so the fixed slope’s expected mean square is not contaminated by the random intercept).

Covariate-adjusted nested inference

  • Added permanova_nested_covariate() (and auto-routing from permanova()): categorical factors in a balanced /-generated hierarchy can now be tested while adjusting for one or more continuous covariates, matching PRIMER’s covariate handling (test the factors “above” the covariate relationship). Each factor’s numerator is adjusted for the covariate; its denominator stays the exact nested expected-mean-square stratum. The covariate is an observation-level nuisance charged to the deepest within-unit residual and tested there, so degrees of freedom partition every observation. A covariate with strong between-unit structure should be split into explicit between- and within-unit predictors. The permanova_nested() error message now names a within-unit continuous covariate as the cause instead of advising contr.sum.
  • Covariate-by-factor interactions are now tested. Writing factor * covariate in a nested design adds the homogeneity-of-slopes term (e.g. Location:Volume), tested over the residual as an observation-level term, with degrees of freedom taken from the residual. Previously such a term was silently dropped and the model collapsed to the additive one. Covariate-by- random interactions (random slopes) remain unsupported: their expected mean squares admit no exact or cleanly constructed denominator.
  • Added decompose_covariate(), a Mundlak-style helper that splits a covariate into between-unit (grouping-unit mean) and within-unit (deviation) parts, so a covariate with strong between-unit structure can be entered as two explicit predictors. The within part is a genuine observation-level covariate for permanova_nested_covariate(); the between part is a unit-level summary.

Unified front door

  • permanova() accepts the dissimilarity on the formula’s left-hand side, permanova(bray ~ treatment + (1 | site), data), matching the vegan::adonis2() idiom; the one-sided ~ terms form with a separate distance argument still works. The assembled PERMANOVA table is exposed as $table on the result.
  • Added permanova(), a single entry point that accepts a formula (with data and distance) or a compiled permanova_design, routes it to the engine matching its random-effect provenance and balance, and returns a result that prints as a PERMANOVA table with a Factors block, denominators, and components of variation. Designs outside every supported envelope stop with a message rather than being approximated.
  • Added type = "I"|"II"|"III" to select the fixed-effect sum-of-squares partition; it is reported as not applicable for designs whose denominator is fixed by the random structure. When called with a formula, permanova() applies sum-to-zero contrasts to the fixed factors on a copy of the data, so Type III (and cross-level factor interactions) give the correct marginal hypotheses without the caller setting contrasts(). A pre-compiled design keeps whatever contrasts it was built with.
  • The PERMANOVA table shows a grand Total row only when the reported sources partition every observation degree of freedom; aggregated-unit engines (random slope, unequal random intercept, unbalanced nested/hybrid) omit it.
  • summary() of a fixed crossed/factorial model now prints the PRIMER-style expected-mean-squares, pseudo-F construction, and components-of-variation blocks. Each term’s EMS coefficient is the trace-derived tr(H Z Z') / df and its component estimate is (MS_term - MS_res) / coefficient; negative estimates are retained.
  • Type II sums of squares now respect marginality instead of rejecting a main effect contained in an interaction. A term is adjusted for every term that does not contain it (the containing interactions are excluded), giving the standard SAS/car/PRIMER “Type II (conditional)” hypothesis; factor SS match car::Anova(type = 2) to numerical tolerance. No additive refit is required.
  • Consolidated the vignette set from 24 example-indexed articles to 8 organised by design family.

Internal checkpoint label: 2.4.0.9000 (unreleased).

Development

  • Preserved the sealed v2.0.0 technical candidate while preparing the publication handoff and the next validated inference phase.
  • Closed Phase 23 external adversarial validation across Phases 19–25. The sealed v2.0.0 and Phase 25 artifacts matched their pinned checksums, all independent scalar/permutation references agreed to machine precision, and the confounded-strata safeguards held.
  • Added an SVD condition-ratio guard for covariate-adjusted contrasts. A numerically near-aliased fixed model now rejects with an actionable package diagnostic before the contrast projector can leak a low-level solve() error; the ratio is retained in adjusted-mean metadata.
  • Phase 25 targets child- and observation-level treatment inference in one unbalanced parent/child hierarchy with explicit unit-scale denominators and within-parent exchangeability contracts.
  • Added permanova_unbalanced_nested_lower() with automatic assignment-level detection, connected-incidence and absolute-scale span guards, exhaustive or Monte Carlo restricted residual permutations, and complete Test Specifications.
  • Extended mixed planned/pairwise contrasts and mixed global-null max-F to the same child- and observation-level unit models.
  • Added scalar GLH and direct permutation reconstruction, a pinned two-level simulation audit, adversarial failure cases, and a Pyrifos occasion vignette.
  • Phase 26 adds unbalanced treatment-by-region/site hybrid inference on equal-site-weight complete profile centroids, with additive region adjustment and region-by-exact-topology profile permutations.
  • Routed mixed planned/pairwise and weak complete-null max-F inference through the same unbalanced profile model and common region reference grid.
  • Added connected-incidence, complete-site-profile, topology-span, residual-df, zero-denominator, and non-Euclidean safeguards plus scalar and exhaustive profile reconstruction tests.
  • Phase 27 adds the narrow correlated (1 + condition | subject) model for balanced complete two-condition repeated measures.
  • Added residual-corrected random intercept–slope trace covariance estimates, optional positive-semidefinite truncation, and exhaustive whole-subject sign-flip inference under an explicit central-symmetry assumption.
  • Added paired-t-squared, scalar covariance, direct sign-flip, asymmetric-null sensitivity, semimetric, and Pyrifos early-versus-late validation.
  • Phase 28 adds permanova_pairwise_strong() for fixed one-factor all-pair complete-distribution equality hypotheses.
  • Every intersection uses a separate sample-size-preserving raw-label action within connected equality components; closed testing then provides strong FWER without assuming subset pivotality.
  • The proof excludes centroid-only nulls with unequal distributions, planned non-pairwise contrasts, dependent observations, and mixed or repeated designs. Exact reconstruction, partial-null preservation, calibration, and a Dune management vignette enforce that boundary.

Internal checkpoint label: 2.0.0 (unreleased).

Validated support-contract consolidation

  • Added permanova_capabilities() and SUPPORT-MATRIX.md as machine- and human-readable maps of every primary inferential engine.
  • Each registry row states its validated design envelope, estimand, denominator, permutation contract, error-control claim, and explicit exclusions; runtime design validators remain authoritative.
  • Extended deterministic and structural release gates to cover the registry, support matrix, public API, all 20 vignettes, and the complete Phase 1–22 documentation sequence.

Internal checkpoint label: 1.8.0 (unreleased).

Mixed-design global-null max-F inference

  • Added permanova_mixed_maxT() and permanova_mixed_maxT_pairwise() for all balanced and unbalanced mixed treatment structures already supported by the mixed-contrast engine.
  • One shared raw experimental-unit permutation stream respects whole-unit, exact-size, hierarchy-topology, block-by-size, or region strata and forms a maximum pseudo-F distribution.
  • Results explicitly claim only weak familywise error control under the complete treatment-null randomization hypothesis.
  • Added exact block enumeration, scalar unit-centroid reconstruction, non-Euclidean coverage, a 5,000-dataset weak-FWER audit, and a Pyrifos dose vignette.

Internal checkpoint label: 1.7.0 (unreleased).

Explicit continuous-covariate adjusted contrasts

  • Every continuous nuisance covariate requires an explicit finite reference value; categorical nuisance factors use declared equal-grid or observed- frequency weighting.
  • Added coefficient-space GLH checks, exhaustive direct Freedman–Lane reconstruction, non-Euclidean coverage, a pinned 500-replicate validation, and a Dune Management-by-A1 vignette.

Internal checkpoint label: 1.6.0 (unreleased).

Unbalanced mixed-design contrasts

Release-candidate hardening

Internal checkpoint label: 1.4.0 (unreleased).

Global-null max-F inference

Internal checkpoint label: 1.3.0 (unreleased).

Mixed-design planned contrasts

Unequal-random-intercept calibration audit

Internal checkpoint label: 1.0.0 (unreleased; not the future stable release).

Planned contrasts and pairwise post-hoc inference

  • Added permanova_contrasts() for user-specified one-df contrasts among the centroids of one categorical fixed factor with unequal group sizes.
  • Each contrast retains all orthogonal group-centroid directions as nuisance structure and receives its own Freedman–Lane residual permutation.
  • Added permanova_pairwise() to construct every pairwise centroid difference. Holm is the default adjustment; Bonferroni, BH, BY, and no adjustment are explicit alternatives.
  • Invalid/non-zero-sum contrast definitions, mixed or multifactor designs, aliases, and zero residual df reject before inference.
  • Added exact constrained-scalar references, non-Euclidean coverage, a pinned null/power validation, and a Dune planned/pairwise vignette.

Internal checkpoint label: 0.9.0 (unreleased).

Unbalanced nested and randomized-block inference

  • Added permanova_unbalanced_nested() for one treatment assigned to top units of an unequal parent/child hierarchy. Equally weighted top centroids exchange only among identical sorted child-count topologies.
  • Added permanova_unbalanced_block() for incomplete and/or unequally replicated randomized blocks with an explicit treatment:block component. Equally weighted intact cell centroids exchange only within block and exact cell-size strata.
  • Both engines require their restricted permutation action to span every treatment contrast and reject disconnected incidence, confounded topology, aliases, or zero residual df.
  • Added exhaustive scalar reconstructions, non-Euclidean tests, a combined operating-characteristic harness, and a Dune unbalanced-mixed vignette.

Internal checkpoint label: 0.8.0 (unreleased).

Unequal-replication random-intercept inference

  • Added permanova_unequal_random_intercept() for one cluster-level categorical treatment and one random intercept with unequal observations per unit.
  • The estimand is explicitly cluster weighted: the analysis uses equally weighted cluster centroids rather than silently giving larger clusters more influence.
  • Freedman–Lane residual permutations move complete cluster centroids only within exact cluster-size strata; those strata must span every treatment contrast.
  • No pooled observation-weighted EMS or parametric F distribution is claimed. Non-Euclidean empirical inference retains the complete Gower spectrum.
  • Added exhaustive scalar references, unsafe-design failures, a Pyrifos vignette, and pinned null/power validation.

Internal checkpoint label: 0.7.0 (unreleased).

Unbalanced fixed-effect inference

  • Added derive_unbalanced_hypotheses() and permanova_unbalanced() for explicit fully estimable Type I, II, or III fixed-effect hypotheses.
  • Type I tests are sequential; additive Type II tests are marginal and order-invariant; Type III tests retain all other terms and require a full-rank model plus explicit sum-to-zero contrasts when interactions occur.
  • Partially estimable terms, aliased incomplete Type III models, Type II main effects contained in interactions, zero residual df, and all random-effect structures reject before inference.
  • Every term uses the common full-model residual denominator and its own Freedman–Lane reduced-model residual permutation.
  • Added exact 5! enumeration, non-Euclidean empirical inference, scalar Type I/II/III references, incomplete-additive coverage, and pinned unequal- cell null/power validation.

Internal checkpoint label: 0.6.0 (unreleased).

Balanced crossed-nested hybrids

  • Added permanova_hybrid() for one fixed treatment crossed with regions and with sites nested within regions.

  • Exact or seeded Monte Carlo permutations move complete treatment-by-region profiles within regions, carrying every site and replicate descendant intact.
  • Added exhaustive profile-permutation references, non-Euclidean inference, strict provenance/balance failures, and pinned null/power validation.

Internal checkpoint label: 0.5.0 (unreleased).

Design-aware multivariate dispersion

  • Added permanova_dispersion() for one categorical fixed target in balanced one-way, single-random-intercept, nested, and canonical randomized-block designs.
  • Distances to group spatial medians are the default; centroids and the equal-group-size bias adjustment are explicit options.
